My chest tightens, my heart races, my hands get sweaty. Sometimes I feel like I can’t catch my breath for a minute or two, like I have to get away right then.

It’s not that I’m thinking anything super specific, it’s more this rush of “something bad” without really knowing what exactly. At home, my wife jokes because I’ll stand there staring at a spider on the wall, sort of frozen, checking it over and over to see if it’s moved, instead of just dealing with it. On my route, if I know a house has lots of webs, I’ll hesitate or take a longer way round, but I still do the job. I keep wondering if I’m overreacting or if there’s something else going on.
D012-D016_h001.question_a:
It sounds a bit ridiculous saying it out loud, but this all started about three years ago and has just got worse. I’m terrified of spiders. Not just “don’t like them” — if I see even a small one, I freeze and my chest tightens straight away. My heart’s pounding, my hands sweat, I feel like I can’t breathe properly and have to get out of the room right then. The reaction is instant, as soon as I spot it.

There’s nothing complicated behind it; it’s the spider itself — how it moves, the legs — that sets me off. I’m not stuck on thoughts about germs or something bad happening later. It’s just that thing in front of me that I can’t cope with.

Because of this, I go out of my way to avoid places where they might be. On my route I try not to go near hedges or old sheds when delivering, and at home I make my wife check the garage or the loft. I know it’s over the top, but I still can’t stop myself from dodging anywhere I think one might be.
D012-D016_h001.question_b:
I’ve been having this thing with spiders for about a year now, maybe a bit more. It’s not just that I don’t like them. What really gets to me are these thoughts that pop in my head, like if I even see a spider or step near where one might be, somehow it’ll crawl on me, lay eggs under my skin, or I’ll bring it home in the mail bag and it’ll hurt my wife or grandkids. I know it sounds irrational, but once it starts, I can’t switch it off.

On my route, if I see a web on a fence or letterbox, my heart jumps straight into my throat. I break out in a sweat, feel shaky, and sometimes I have to just stop and steady myself. Then I start doing these little rituals—checking my shoes over and over, shaking out the mailbag multiple times, avoiding certain houses, even going back to re-check the van to “make sure” there’s no spider inside. If I try not to do these checks, the anxiety just keeps building until I give in and do them.
